title: Joining Cab Calloway and recording The Hi-De-Ho Man
summary: Hired when Kansas Fields left, he played on the film soundtrack and a first Cab record date, and remembers Cab's speech 'Get what you need'.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: We played the Savoy, so I was up there for six more months with Willie Bryant. We played the Savoy. And then, that's when I heard from Cab Calloway -- a drummer that was with him, Kansas Fields, I think was playing drums for him at the time, and he was looking for a drummer, and this was when I made -- he was getting ready to do a movie at the time when I joined the band, "The Hide Ho Man" up in the Bronx, he was doing it -- called "The Hide Ho Man", and that's when I joined the band and we made the record
of "The Hidy Ho Man", that's me. I'll never forget that -- that was a big thrill for me.
That was the last part of '47 -- around December, I think -- '46, not '47; the last part of '46. He hadn't -- it hadn't been Christmas yet when I joined. He was up there making a picture.
Yeah, "The Hidy Ho Man". Yeah, I was playing drums, and I made the recording on the soundtrack and on it.
Then I made my first record date with him, also, with Cab, during that same time, because the band was getting ready to go out on the road.
You mean the first recording with Cab?

Yeah, my first recording. That's where I made "Necessity", "The Hidy Ho Man", "That's Me"; "The Calloway Boogie" and I forgot what the other tune was, but we did four sides that day at the theatre there at 52nd Street and Broadway. We were recording at the theatre there, and the A&R man was Mitchell Ayres, I think, and Mitchell Ayres was there. That's when Cab made his speech, which I never forgot because I was very much impressed with it when he said, "Fellows, we're getting ready to go out on the road, and we'll be out for three
months. Don't get what you want; get what you need!" And I always remembered that speech, I never forgot it. That really stayed with me.
